newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares rise, brokers busy with new system.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares rise, brokers busy with new system.

text.p: The Egyptian all-share index hit a 17-month high on Sunday but brokers said the rise was misleading and they were too busy grappling with the technical problems connected with a new dealing an clearing system.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index rose 0.40 points to 235.19, its highest since April 1995, on low turnover of 28.6 million pounds ($8.4 million).
But the most active shares closed mixed and several flour milling shares fell back from recent highs.

Turnover was also artificially swollen by the listing of almost 360,000 shares in Arab Drugs and Chemical Industries, 30 percent of the company's equity, at 40.00 pounds a share. The transaction was the result of another partial privatisation.

On its first full day of trading, newly privatised Upper Egypt Flour Mills rose strongly to 45.50 from the sale price of 40.00 pounds. But Central and West Delta Flour Mills, the busiest stock, ended unchanged at 47.60, and two other millers lost some of their post-privatisation gains.
Among other very active stocks, Commercial International Bank dropped 1.50 to 468.75 and Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries lost 2.00 to end the day at 157.00 pounds.

Youssef Khalil of Delta EAB stockbrokers said a system of codes for clients may be helping prices upwards because it made it much easier to buy than to sell. "It's one of the reasons the market has been going up," he said.
But Mohamed Hossny, vice president of Triple A Securities, said a much bigger problem was the transition to a new clearing and bookkeeping system, expected to go live this week.
"Everyone's not so interested in the market right now, but in this. The coordination is going to be horrendous," he said.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 368.44 points from 368.65 on Thursday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 161.42 from 160.92.
